g.text: The default actuator is the wrong shape, not just the wrong size

text.style: font-size: 11.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Avenir Next', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #a8a8a7

g.text: Continuous torque as a share of peak. Real motors sustain a fraction of their peak; the PD-with-torque-clamp

text.style: font-size: 11.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Avenir Next', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #a8a8a7

font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Avenir Next', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #a8a8a7

g.text: A flat clamp implies a motor that holds its peak forever. No motor does. The clamp is generous at steady state and pessimistic in transient.
